name: Laboratory sea-ice growth from natural seawater in a ~1 m3 tank inside a walk-in freezer at -15, -25 and -40 C (carbonate system and CO2 fluxes)
plain_name: Grow a metre-sized block of sea ice in a walk-in freezer to follow its carbon
description: Filtered, UV-sterilized open-ocean seawater in a 105 x 95 x 99 cm tank is frozen from the surface in a walk-in freezer (Institute of Ocean Sciences, Sidney BC) at ambient temperatures of -15, -25 or -40 C until the ice is about 20 cm thick (1.8-22.5 days), to relate growth rate to inorganic carbon rejection.
keywords: Grow a metre-sized block of sea ice in a walk-in freezer to follow its carbon

sources.citation: Konig, Miller, Simpson and Vagle (2018) Carbon Dynamics During the Formation of Sea Ice at Different Growth Rates, Frontiers in Earth Science 6:234

reported_equipment: walk-in freezer with three refrigeration condensers (Institute of Ocean Sciences, Sidney, BC)

requirements.rationale: The freezer air must be held at each of -15, -25 and -40 C (258.15 to 233.15 K).
The cold space must take the 99 cm tall seawater tank.
Circumscribed diameter of the 105 x 95 cm tank footprint is sqrt(105^2+95^2) = 141.6 cm (rounded up to 1416 mm).

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
